set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is the expected course of cellulitis on antibiotic therapy?
opts: It improves visibly within hours, fever resolves within six hours, and erythema clears within three days
That is faster than the described course.
It worsens for the first week before any improvement, with fever expected to persist throughout
Fever persisting beyond forty-eight hours is a reason to change therapy.
It resolves without any change in appearance, since the erythema is not caused by the infection
The erythema is part of the infection.
It may look worse on day one, fever usually resolves within twenty-four hours, inflammation over one to two weeks
Correct. Fever beyond forty-eight hours prompts a change guided by culture.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which finding in a woman with persistent acne points toward polycystic ovarian syndrome?
opts: Pustules pierced by a central hair over the thighs and trunk
That points toward folliculitis.
Premenstrual flares of acne with an otherwise normal cycle
Premenstrual flares are a common feature of ordinary acne.
Hirsutism together with irregular or absent menses
Correct. That combination indicates androgen hypersecretion.
Flushing with hot drinks and visible facial telangiectasias
That points toward rosacea instead.

set1.io: a — Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing, management, referrals, patient education and prognosis of cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which slides did Professor Jaquith name out loud as really important, and what are they?
opts: The cellulitis versus erysipelas comparison
Important content, but not the slides she flagged.
The necrotizing fasciitis red flags
Not the slides she flagged.
The acne treatment ladder, slides 32 and 33
Correct — she said 'make sure you know this', which is as direct a flag as the lecture gives.
The MRSA risk factor list, slides 44 and 45
Not the slides she named.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which class is the typical first-line topical therapy for comedonal and inflammatory acne?
opts: Topical antimicrobials, which act against Cutibacterium acnes in the follicle
Those are used with benzoyl peroxide but are not comedolytic.
Topical dapsone gel, which is anti-inflammatory by an unknown mechanism
Dapsone gel is an option but not the typical first-line choice.
Topical azelaic acid, which is antimicrobial, comedolytic and anti-inflammatory
Azelaic acid is approved by the Food and Drug Administration for rosacea only.
Topical retinoids, which are comedolytic and normalise hyperkeratinisation
Correct — adapalene, tazarotene and tretinoin, generally the most effective for mild disease.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How does acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis present after impetigo?
opts: Migratory arthritis, a new heart murmur and subcutaneous nodules over the elbows
That describes acute rheumatic fever.
Fever with a sandpaper rash, strawberry tongue and circumoral pallor
That describes scarlet fever.
Painless jaundice with pale stools and progressive weight loss
That picture is unrelated to this complication.
Sudden oedema, haematuria with smoky or tea-coloured urine, proteinuria and hypertension
Correct — especially in three to seven year olds.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is the typical timing and distribution of hot tub folliculitis?
opts: Onset three to seven days after a sore throat, on the face and extremities
That timing belongs to post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis after impetigo.
Onset eight hours to five days after exposure, on the trunk, extremities and buttocks
Correct. It usually spares the face, neck, soles and palms.
Onset two to five days after trauma, around the fingernail folds of the hand
That is the timing and site of acute paronychia.
Onset within forty-eight hours, on the lower extremity with a demarcated border
That describes erysipelas.

set1.io: a — Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing, management, referrals, patient education and prognosis of cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Professor Jaquith said to write Bactroban as the ointment rather than the cream. Why?
opts: The cream causes more contact irritation on inflamed skin
Irritation was not the reason she gave.
The cream is not licensed for use on the face
No licensing restriction was described.
The cream costs far more and is never covered
Correct — roughly a hundred times the price, and the ointment is covered. A prescribing detail that appears on no slide.
The cream is less effective against Staphylococcus aureus
The reason she gave was cost and coverage, not potency.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What causes hot tub folliculitis and why does it occur?
opts: Streptococcus pyogenes, a Gram-positive organism, from a break in the skin
That organism causes erysipelas and non-bullous impetigo.
Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a Gram-negative organism, from inadequately chlorinated water
Correct. Whirlpools, hot tubs, water slides and physiotherapy pools are the named sources.
Staphylococcus aureus, a Gram-positive organism, from shared towels and razors
That organism causes ordinary bacterial folliculitis.
Corynebacterium minutissimum, a Gram-positive organism, from heat and humidity
That organism causes erythrasma in intertriginous skin.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Describe the classic appearance of non-bullous impetigo.
opts: A vesicle over inflamed skin deepens into a dermal ulcer with a thick grey-yellow crust
That is ecthyma.
Papules and pustules on an erythematous base, each pierced by a single central hair
That is folliculitis.
A macule evolves into a vesicle or pustule that ruptures, leaving a honey-coloured adherent crust
Correct, typically on the face and extremities, with regional lymphadenopathy common.
Tense clear or cloudy bullae appear on intact skin and leave a collarette after they rupture
That is bullous impetigo.

set1.io: c — Differentiate primary from secondary bacterial infection of the skin
set1.q: Which portals of entry are named for cellulitis?
opts: Tinea pedis, open lesion, trauma, surgical wound, insect bite, fissure and radiation therapy
Correct. Those are distinct from the risk factors, which include diabetes and lymphoedema.
Nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus, shaving, occlusive clothing and hot humid weather
Those are risk factors for folliculitis and furuncles.
Manicure, ingrown nail, hangnail and nail biting affecting the soft tissue of the finger
Those are predisposing factors for acute paronychia.
Contaminated whirlpools, hot tubs, water slides and inadequately chlorinated pools
Those are the exposures for Pseudomonas folliculitis.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: When can cellulitis be managed without any diagnostic workup?
opts: Limited area of involvement, minimal pain, no systemic signs and no risk factor for serious illness
Correct. Serious infections warrant blood cultures, punch biopsy, blood count and creatine phosphokinase.
Any case in which the patient is afebrile, regardless of the extent of the affected area
Extent of involvement and risk factors both matter, not fever alone.
Any case occurring in a patient under fifty years of age with no history of diabetes
Age and diabetes are two considerations among several.
Only after blood cultures have returned negative and inflammatory markers are normal
The point is that no workup is needed in that group at all.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What causes chronic paronychia and who is at risk?
opts: A bacterial infection of the soft tissue around the nail, with Staphylococcus aureus commonest
That describes acute paronychia.
A dermatophyte infection of the nail plate itself, with Trichophyton rubrum commonest
That describes onychomycosis, one of the differentials.
A foreign body reaction to a cut hair entering the skin, commonest in those who shave
That describes pseudofolliculitis barbae.
An inflammatory reaction of the proximal nail fold to irritants and allergens, with Candida albicans commonest
Correct — diabetics, laundry workers, cleaners, cooks, bartenders, dishwashers and swimmers.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is chronic paronychia treated?
opts: Topical mupirocin applied to the nail fold three times daily until the swelling settles
Mupirocin is an antibacterial used for impetigo and staphylococcal carriage.
Keep the hands dry and use a broad-spectrum topical antifungal, with oral fluconazole in severe cases
Correct — treat the underlying inflammation and infection together.
Warm soaks three times daily with incision and drainage if purulent material has collected
That is the treatment of acute paronychia.
Oral cephalexin for ten days with removal of the nail plate if there is no early response
Antibacterial therapy does not address the usual candidal cause.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: A patient with folliculitis has not responded to a topical antibiotic and the infection is now extensive. Which oral agents apply?
opts: Doxycycline or minocycline
Those are the oral tetracyclines used in acne.
Cephalexin or dicloxacillin
Correct — trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin or linezolid if resistance is suspected.
Penicillin V or amoxicillin
Those are not the agents named for extensive folliculitis.
Erythromycin or clarithromycin
Those are the agents for widespread erythrasma.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which laboratory abnormalities are common in erysipelas, and what do they contribute?
opts: Thrombocytopenia with mild hyponatraemia and transaminitis — and diagnostic in almost every case
That is the Rocky Mountain spotted fever pattern.
Eosinophilia with a raised immunoglobulin E — diagnostic when combined with the rash
That pattern is not described for erysipelas.
Entirely normal inflammatory markers — which is what confirms the diagnosis
Inflammatory markers are commonly raised.
Leukocytosis with raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein — common but not diagnostic
Correct. The diagnosis remains clinical in a classic presentation.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What defines folliculitis?
opts: Inflammatory cells within the wall and ostia of the hair follicle, forming a follicular pustule
Correct. The causes include infection, physical injury and chemical irritation.
A deep-seated abscess of the hair follicle and the adjacent subcutaneous tissue
That defines a furuncle.
Inflammation of the cutaneous apocrine glands of the axilla, groin or perineum
That defines hidradenitis suppurativa.
A foreign body reaction to a cut hair that curves back into the wall of the follicle
That defines pseudofolliculitis barbae.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which laboratory and imaging studies are appropriate in classic erysipelas?
opts: None routinely — the diagnosis is clinical, and blood and tissue cultures have very low yield
Correct. Leukocytosis and raised inflammatory markers are common but not diagnostic.
Blood and tissue cultures in every case, since organism identification guides the antibiotic
Their yield is described as extremely low and not cost effective.
Computed tomography of the affected limb to define the depth of tissue involvement
Imaging is of low yield and not indicated in classic presentation.
Punch biopsy of the leading edge to distinguish erysipelas from contact dermatitis
Biopsy is not part of the routine erysipelas workup.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Where should a patient with necrotizing fasciitis be admitted?
opts: A surgical intensive care unit, ideally a burn or trauma centre
Correct — a team approach with consultations is required.
A general medical ward with hourly observations
That level of care is inadequate for this condition.
A dermatology inpatient unit for wound management
The disease is deeper than skin and needs surgical care.
An ambulatory unit for daily dressing changes and review
That is far below the level of care required.

set1.io: d — Medical care strategies across infant, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: What isolation advice is given for a child with impetigo?
opts: Isolate until treatment has been underway for twenty-four to forty-eight hours
Correct, and do not share towels, clothing, bath water, washcloths or razors.
Isolate until every crusted lesion has completely healed and the skin is clear
The stated interval is tied to starting treatment, not to healing.
No isolation is needed at any point, since impetigo does not spread person to person
Impetigo is described as very contagious and autoinoculable.
Isolate for a full ten days from the appearance of the very first crusted lesion
That is longer than the interval given.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which layers does cellulitis involve, and which organisms cause it?
opts: The superficial epidermis alone, from Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes
That describes impetigo.
The stratum corneum of intertriginous skin, from Corynebacterium minutissimum
That describes erythrasma.
The deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue, from Group A streptococci or Staphylococcus aureus
Correct. It may be purulent or non-purulent, which changes the antibiotic choice.
The upper dermis and superficial lymphatics, almost always from Group A streptococci
That describes erysipelas.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Where does erythrasma most commonly appear?
opts: Lower extremity in most patients, almost never affecting both legs
That is the distribution of cellulitis.
Inner thighs, crural region, scrotum, and between the fourth and fifth toes
Correct. Less common sites are the axilla, under the breasts and intergluteal folds.
Back of the neck, face, axillae and buttocks, favouring areas of friction
That is the distribution of furuncles and carbuncles.
Face and extremities, spreading by scratching and self-inoculation
That is the distribution of non-bullous impetigo.

set1.io: b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
set1.q: In whom did Professor Jaquith say pseudofolliculitis barbae most commonly occurs?
opts: Adolescents of any background during puberty
Age was not the factor she described.
Black and brown males, or anyone with curlier facial or body hair
Correct — hair curvature is the mechanism, not hygiene, and she called it very common.
Fair-skinned males who shave daily with a multi-blade razor
Skin tone is not the driver; hair curvature is.
Females who wax rather than shave
Not the group she named.

set1.io: b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: How does purulence change the antibiotic choice in cellulitis?
opts: Purulent cellulitis prompts cover for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
Correct — trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, doxycycline, clindamycin or linezolid.
Purulent cellulitis prompts a switch to penicillin V to cover Group A streptococcus
Penicillin V is the erysipelas treatment.
Purulent cellulitis prompts topical mupirocin in addition to the oral antibiotic
Topical mupirocin is used in impetigo and for nasal decolonisation.
Purulent cellulitis prompts oral fluconazole because yeast is likely to be present
Antifungal therapy belongs to chronic paronychia.

set1.io: b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: When should cultures be obtained in impetigo?
opts: Only when the lesions have failed to respond after a full two-week course of topical mupirocin
Culture is directed by resistance risk and complications, not treatment duration.
Only in children under three years of age, since they are the group at highest risk of complications
Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis particularly affects three to seven year olds.
When the patient is at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, or when post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is present
Correct — a health-care worker or teacher is the example given of high risk.
In every case at first presentation, since staphylococcal and streptococcal disease are treated differently from one another
Impetigo is most often diagnosed by clinical appearance alone.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which feature distinguishes contact dermatitis from cellulitis?
opts: Warmth and tenderness with a rapidly expanding border
Those are the features of cellulitis itself.
A raised plaque with a sharply demarcated edge
That points to erysipelas.
Pain out of proportion to the physical examination
That points to necrotizing fasciitis.
Itching and vesicles with an absence of fever
Correct — cellulitis is tender and warm rather than itchy.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is hidradenitis suppurativa and where does it occur?
opts: Inflammation of the eccrine sweat glands, most often on the palms, soles and the axillary vault
Eccrine glands are the ones involved in hyperhidrosis, not this condition.
Infection of the upper third of the stratum corneum in intertriginous skin under heat and humidity
That describes erythrasma.
Infection of the hair follicle extending into the adjacent subcutaneous fat of the neck and back
That describes a furuncle.
Inflammation of cutaneous apocrine glands, most often in the axilla, and also groin, breasts or perineum
Correct. It is also called acne inversa because it resembles acne vulgaris.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How does a carbuncle differ from a furuncle at presentation?
opts: It presents as a plaque raised above the skin with a demarcated edge
That describes erysipelas.
It is extremely painful and more often produces malaise, chills and fever
Correct. Systemic symptoms are more common with a carbuncle.
It is painless and produces no systemic symptoms of any kind at all
Carbuncles are described as extremely painful.
It presents as a single opening with a surrounding zone of erythema
That is the furuncle. Carbuncles have sieve-like multiple openings.

set1.io: b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: Which trait is shared by the oral agents named across this lecture for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infection?
opts: Penicillin V, erythromycin and clarithromycin recur as the core options
Those cover streptococcal and corynebacterial infection.
Mupirocin, retapamulin and fusidic acid recur as the core options
Those are topical agents rather than oral ones.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, clindamycin and doxycycline recur as the core options
Correct, with linezolid and ciprofloxacin added in particular settings.
Dicloxacillin, cephalexin and amoxicillin-clavulanate recur as the core options
Those are the agents for methicillin-sensitive disease.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is acute paronychia treated?
opts: Warm soaks for twenty minutes three times daily in mild cases; incision and drainage in severe cases
Correct, with oral antibiotics and cultures to rule out resistant organisms where appropriate.
A broad-spectrum topical antifungal in all cases, with oral fluconazole if the disease is severe
That is the treatment of chronic paronychia.
Immediate nail plate removal in all cases, since the nail harbours the responsible organism
Nail removal is not the described treatment.
Oral antibiotics alone in all cases, since incision of the nail fold risks permanent deformity
Incision and drainage is used in severe cases.

set1.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What level of the skin does impetigo infect, and which organisms cause it?
opts: An infection of the tissue surrounding muscle and fascia, usually polymicrobial in nature
That describes necrotizing fasciitis.
A superficial epidermal infection, most often Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes
Correct. It is very contagious and autoinoculable, and common in infants and children.
An infection of the upper dermis and superficial lymphatics, most often Streptococcus pyogenes
That describes erysipelas.
An infection of the deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue, streptococcal or staphylococcal
That describes cellulitis.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which conditions are named in the differential for bullous impetigo?
opts: Varicella, insect bites, herpes simplex, tinea corporis and scabies
That is the differential for non-bullous impetigo.
Deep vein thrombosis, discoid lupus and cellulitis of the limb
That is the differential for erysipelas.
Cystic acne, folliculitis and hidradenitis suppurativa
That is the differential for furunculosis and carbuncles.
Thermal burn, allergic contact dermatitis, and herpes simplex or zoster
Correct — non-bullous impetigo has a different differential list.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How does acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis present after impetigo?
opts: Gradual weight loss, painless jaundice, pale stools and dark urine over several weeks
That picture is unrelated to this complication.
Fever with a sandpaper rash, strawberry tongue and circumoral pallor within days
That describes scarlet fever rather than this renal complication.
Migratory joint pain, a new heart murmur and subcutaneous nodules over the elbows
That describes acute rheumatic fever.
Sudden oedema, haematuria with smoky or tea-coloured urine, proteinuria and hypertension
Correct, especially in three to seven year olds.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which tests may be used in acute paronychia and what does each exclude?
opts: Wood's lamp for coral-red fluorescence, potassium hydroxide for dermatophytes, biopsy for malignancy
Wood's lamp examination is the test for erythrasma.
Blood cultures for bacteraemia, creatine phosphokinase for muscle damage, imaging for osteomyelitis
That workup belongs to serious cellulitis.
Nasal swab for staphylococcal carriage, plucked hair for dermatophytes, biopsy for follicular disease
That workup belongs to resistant folliculitis.
Gram stain and culture for the bacterial cause, potassium hydroxide for candida, Tzanck smear for herpetic whitlow
Correct. It is usually a clinical diagnosis, so testing is directed rather than routine.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Describe the physical findings of a carbuncle.
opts: Several loculated abscesses, superficial pustules, necrotic plugs and sieve-like draining openings
Correct — a deeper infection made of interconnecting furuncles in several follicles.
A single firm tender nodule with one opening and a surrounding zone of erythema and swelling
That is the furuncle rather than the carbuncle.
Nodules, sinus tracts and meshlike scarring in the axilla or the perineum
That describes hidradenitis suppurativa.
A well-demarcated raised plaque with red streaks extending toward a lymph node
That describes erysipelas with lymphatic involvement.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What are the examination findings of cellulitis?
opts: Tense bullae with purple fluid and skin that has become insensate over the affected area
Those are the late findings of necrotizing fasciitis.
All four cardinal signs of inflammation, most often on one lower leg, with borders neither raised nor demarcated
Correct. Bilateral disease is described as almost never occurring.
All four cardinal signs of inflammation, most often bilateral, with a sharply raised and demarcated edge
A raised demarcated border points to erysipelas, and bilateral disease is atypical.
Painless erythema with scaling at the border, most often over intertriginous skin surfaces
That picture suggests a dermatophyte infection instead.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the hallmark lesion of acne vulgaris on physical examination?
opts: The comedone, either open (blackhead) or closed (whitehead)
Correct. Acne is polymorphic, but the comedone is what defines it.
The pustule, sitting on an erythematous base around a central hair
That is the lesion of folliculitis.
The nodule, deep-seated and arising in several adjacent follicles
Nodules occur in acne but the hallmark is the comedone.
The papule, small and inflamed without any surface keratin plug
Papules occur in acne but they are not what defines it.

set2.io: a — Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing, management, referrals, patient education and prognosis of cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the microbiology of necrotizing fasciitis, as Professor Jaquith described it?
opts: Always methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
Resistance is not what defines this infection.
Polymicrobial from mixed flora, or group A Streptococcus
Correct — aerobic or anaerobic. She introduced it as the flesh-eating bacteria.
Always monomicrobial Staphylococcus aureus
The infection is described as polymicrobial or group A streptococcal.
Always Pseudomonas aeruginosa from water exposure
Pseudomonas is the hot tub folliculitis organism in this lecture.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which shaving advice is given for pseudofolliculitis barbae?
opts: Continue the current routine and treat each papule with a topical antibiotic
The shaving technique itself has to change.
Stop shaving if possible, use clean razors, and avoid lift-and-cut razor systems
Correct — mild razor angles and single or at most double blades are preferred.
Shave daily against the grain with a multi-blade razor to cut hairs below the surface
Cutting hair below the surface is what allows it to re-enter the skin.
Shave weekly with an electric razor set to the closest possible cutting length
The closest cut is the problem rather than the solution.

set2.io: b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Which measure is recommended when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is a concern in a drained furuncle?
opts: Start linezolid empirically before any material is obtained
Empiric therapy uses dicloxacillin or cephalexin unless resistance is suspected.
Swab the nasal vestibule of every household contact first
Nasal swabbing is described for recurrent folliculitis.
Defer drainage until the culture result becomes available
Drainage is not delayed for culture.
Culture the material obtained at incision and drainage
Correct, and give endocarditis prophylaxis to at-risk patients.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is a furuncle?
opts: An infection of the upper dermis extending into superficial skin lymphatics
That is erysipelas.
A deep-seated abscess of a hair follicle and the adjacent subcutaneous tissue
Correct. Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest organism.
An inflammation of the follicle wall and ostia forming a superficial pustule
That is folliculitis, which is confined to the follicle.
A collection of purulent material seeded by traumatic inoculation of bacteria
That is an abscess, which arises from inoculation rather than a follicle.

set2.io: b, c & d — MRSA, primary versus secondary infection, and care across the age range
set2.q: What is Professor Jaquith's simplified default when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is suspected?
opts: Cephalexin alone at a higher dose
Cephalexin is the standard agent, but it does not cover the resistant organism.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole double strength alone
She described adding it to cephalexin rather than replacing it.
Intravenous vancomycin as an outpatient
That is not the oral outpatient default she described.
Cephalexin plus trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
Correct — double strength, and the combination is broad enough to cover before susceptibilities return, which then confirm.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What should be suspected when acne scarring seems out of proportion to the severity of lesions?
opts: An underlying immunodeficiency impairing the healing of each lesion
That is not among the explanations the lecture offers.
Patient manipulation of the lesions through picking or squeezing
Correct. Patients and families are educated about that risk.
An undiagnosed hyperandrogenic state driving deeper inflammation
Hyperandrogenism is suspected from hirsutism and menstrual irregularity.
Resistance of Cutibacterium acnes to the prescribed antimicrobial
Resistance would show as failure to improve, not disproportionate scarring.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which specimens are taken in serious cellulitis?
opts: Perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence
That investigates autoimmune blistering disease.
A potassium hydroxide preparation of the leading edge
That would investigate a fungal cause.
Blood cultures and a skin punch biopsy
Correct, alongside a complete blood count and creatine phosphokinase.
A superficial swab of the intact affected skin
A surface swab is not among the described tests.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Where does acne vulgaris rank among skin diseases in the United States?
opts: It is the second most common, affecting about 40% of Americans in their lifetime
The lecture ranks it first, at roughly twice that figure.
It is the most common in adolescents only, affecting about 20% of adults
The 80% figure is a lifetime prevalence across the population.
It is uncommon overall, affecting fewer than 10% of Americans in their lifetime
That substantially understates the stated prevalence.
It is the most common skin disease, affecting about 80% of Americans in their lifetime
Correct. It usually begins with the onset of puberty.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How does the lecture describe the definitive procedure for an abscess that will not drain?
opts: Surgical incision and drainage, covered in detail in a later course
Correct — the aim is to eradicate infection and prevent recurrence.
Wide excision of the affected area under general anaesthesia
That belongs to hidradenitis suppurativa.
Aspiration with a fine needle under ultrasound guidance
That is not the described procedure.
Observation with warm soaks until it drains on its own
That applies to a lesion that has already drained.

set2.io: b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Why will antibiotics not work on the devitalised area in a cellulitic limb?
opts: The organism in devitalised tissue is always methicillin resistant
The problem is delivery rather than resistance.
Devitalised tissue destroys antibiotic molecules on contact
That is not the described mechanism.
Oral antibiotics never reach the subcutaneous tissue at all
They do, where the tissue is perfused.
It is not perfused, so the drug never reaches the site
Correct — tense, cyanotic, necrotic, bronzed or blanched tissue needs debridement.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is a carbuncle?
opts: A furuncle that has become secondarily infected with yeast
Secondary yeast infection is not what defines it.
A furuncle that has failed to respond to oral antibiotics
Treatment response is not part of the definition.
Two or more confluent furuncles with separate heads
Correct — interconnecting furuncles arising in several hair follicles.
A single furuncle larger than five millimetres across
Size alone does not make a furuncle a carbuncle.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the diagnostic finding in erythrasma?
opts: Coral-red fluorescence under a Wood's lamp
Correct. That is what separates it from tinea and candidiasis clinically.
Green fluorescence under a Wood's lamp
The colour described is coral-red.
Branching hyphae on a potassium hydroxide mount
That would indicate a dermatophyte infection instead.
Gram-positive cocci in chains on a Gram stain
That appearance suggests streptococcal infection.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the natural course of hot tub folliculitis?
opts: Chronic and relapsing for months after a single exposure
The condition clears within days.
Resolving only after the affected follicles are drained
Drainage is not part of the management.
Usually self-limiting, clearing in two to ten days
Correct — ciprofloxacin is reserved for widespread or resistant cases.
Progressive without oral ciprofloxacin in every patient
Most cases resolve without specific treatment.

set2.io: d — Medical care strategies across infant, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set2.q: Which oral antibiotic is described as the drug of choice for impetigo in children?
opts: Dicloxacillin
It is listed as an option but not the paediatric drug of choice.
Erythromycin
It is not the agent named for children here.
Cephalexin
Correct. Clindamycin is used where there is penicillin allergy.
Doxycycline
Doxycycline is limited to children over eight years old.

set2.q: Where and after what does Professor Jaquith say she sees folliculitis most often?
opts: The groin, after shaving
Correct — hot tubs come second, and hot tub folliculitis is the Pseudomonas one.
The scalp, after using hair oils
Not the site or trigger she named.
The lower legs, after swimming in fresh water
Fresh-water exposure is cercarial dermatitis in a different lecture.
The face, after using an occlusive moisturiser
Not the site or trigger she named.

set2.io: a — Compare and contrast the etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, clinical manifestations, differential diagnosis, diagnostic testing, management, referrals, patient education and prognosis of cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Professor Jaquith treats a small-surface-area non-purulent cellulitis as an outpatient. What follow-up does she insist on, and why?
opts: No routine follow-up unless the patient deteriorates
She described a mandatory review rather than safety-netting alone.
Return in 72 hours for repeat blood cultures
Blood cultures belong to the emergency department work-up she described separately.
Return in 24 to 48 hours, because it spreads so fast
Correct — to confirm the antibiotic is working. That interval is the safety net on outpatient treatment.
Return in one week, once the course is complete
A week is far longer than the interval she gave.

set2.io: b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Which oral agents are named for folliculitis when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is cultured or suspected?
opts: Doxycycline, minocycline or sarecycline
Those are the oral tetracyclines used in acne.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin or linezolid
Correct. Cephalexin and dicloxacillin cover the methicillin-sensitive organism.
Cephalexin, dicloxacillin or amoxicillin-clavulanate
Those cover methicillin-sensitive disease rather than the resistant organism.
Penicillin V, clindamycin or erythromycin base
Penicillin V is the erysipelas treatment.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which layer does erysipelas involve, and which organism causes it?
opts: The upper dermis and superficial cutaneous lymphatics, most often Group A streptococcus
Correct. It is a superficial cellulitis of the dermal layer.
The deeper dermis and subcutaneous tissue, most often Staphylococcus aureus
That describes cellulitis rather than erysipelas.
The superficial epidermis only, most often Streptococcus pyogenes or staphylococci
That describes impetigo.
The fascia surrounding muscle and nerve, most often a polymicrobial mixture
That describes necrotizing fasciitis.

set2.q: On the ladder she flagged, what is added for MODERATE acne with pustules?
opts: Azelaic acid used on its own as a single topical
Azelaic acid is the alternative when a topical retinoid is not tolerated in mild disease.
A topical retinoid, an ORAL antibiotic, and benzoyl peroxide
Correct — the severe tier is the same three, or oral isotretinoin instead.
A topical retinoid and benzoyl peroxide, with no oral agent
That is the mild mixed tier; moderate adds an oral antibiotic.
Oral isotretinoin used as the sole agent from the outset
Isotretinoin is the severe tier.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which preventive measures are advised in hidradenitis suppurativa?
opts: Avoid heat, cleanse daily with antibacterial soap or benzoyl peroxide wash, lose weight, stop smoking
Correct, along with avoiding constrictive clothing and considering laser hair removal.
Avoid all water contact, apply a barrier ointment daily, gain weight and use an occlusive dressing
None of those measures is recommended for this condition.
Shower immediately after any hot tub use and monitor the disinfectant levels in the water
Those are the preventive measures for Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Avoid sharing towels or razors and isolate from school until treatment has been underway
Those are the patient education points for impetigo.

set2.io: b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Which oral antibiotics are used for furuncles and carbuncles when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is cultured or suspected?
opts: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, clindamycin or doxycycline
Correct. Empiric therapy for the sensitive organism is dicloxacillin or cephalexin.
Dicloxacillin, cephalexin or amoxicillin-clavulanate
Those are the empiric agents for methicillin-sensitive disease.
Penicillin V, erythromycin or clarithromycin
Penicillin V is used for erysipelas and the macrolides for erythrasma.
Ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin or moxifloxacin
Ciprofloxacin is named for resistant Pseudomonas folliculitis.

set2.io: a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How should laboratory tests and imaging be sequenced in suspected necrotizing fasciitis?
opts: They should be repeated at forty-eight hours, because early results are usually uninformative
The urgency is immediate, not at forty-eight hours.
They should not delay surgical intervention, because this is a surgical emergency with high mortality
Correct. Blood count, chemistry, arterial blood gas, urinalysis and cultures are all sent.
They should be completed and reviewed before surgery, because the findings determine the incision
Investigation must not delay operative treatment.
They should replace surgery where imaging is negative, because operating carries its own risk
Negative imaging does not exclude the diagnosis.

set2.io: c — Differentiate primary from secondary bacterial infection of the skin
set2.q: What is the primary portal of entry for impetigo?
opts: A hair follicle already inflamed by shaving or occlusive clothing
That mechanism belongs to folliculitis and furuncles.
Traumatic inoculation of bacteria deep into the dermal tissues
That mechanism describes abscess formation.
Minor superficial breaks in the skin such as cuts and bug bites
Correct. No predisposing lesion is identified in most patients.
An occluded apocrine duct that ruptures into the surrounding dermis
That mechanism belongs to hidradenitis suppurativa.

set2.q: Which two combination topical products are named for reducing antibiotic resistance in acne?
opts: Cleocin T (clindamycin with salicylic acid) and Erygel (erythromycin with salicylic acid)
Those brand names refer to single-agent topical antibiotics.
Altabax (retapamulin with mupirocin) and Bactroban (mupirocin with benzoyl peroxide)
Those are single-agent impetigo treatments, not acne combinations.
BenzaClin (clindamycin with benzoyl peroxide) and Benzamycin (erythromycin with benzoyl peroxide)
Correct. Both pair a topical antibiotic with benzoyl peroxide.
Differin (adapalene with benzoyl peroxide) and Tazorac (tazarotene with benzoyl peroxide)
Those brand names refer to single-agent retinoids.
